note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found on chest imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents after being evaluated by PCP for a cough diagnosed as bronchitis. Chest X-ray was performed to rule out pneumonia and incidentally found a lung nodule. CT scan confirmed the finding, and patient was referred to thoracic surgery. Patient reports a cough that has been intermittent for approximately three months, initially noticed after spending a day loading hay while working with horses. Patient subsequently developed a cold which prompted the PCP visit. The cough has since resolved. Patient reports being active with regular biking and notes that he typically does not get sick. Patient expresses anxiety about the diagnosis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any pain, shortness of breath, or dyspnea on exertion.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No previous history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a previous smoker who quit approximately seven years ago. Patient exercises regularly and bikes frequently on trail systems. Patient works with horses.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 124/76, heart rate 70, respiratory rate 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart regular rate and rhythm without clicks, rubs, or murmurs. No extra beats appreciated. Extremities: skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema to lower extremities. Mild swelling noted at knuckles of third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT shows solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in lateral aspect of right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule, incidentally found. Plan: Pulmonary function tests to establish baseline lung function. PET CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery planned for nodule removal with small portion of lung, under general anesthesia, approximately 1.5 hours duration. Patient will be admitted post-procedure with chest tube until post-operative day 1, anticipated hospital stay one night. Continue rheumatoid arthritis management with rheumatologist follow-up and continuation of current methotrexate therapy.
